artifacts.notes: Extent as the retrieving lane measured it: Complete page master image, The Progressive Farmer 1889-01-15 ed-1 page 8, 6576x9787 px 8-bit greyscale; the highest resolution the Library of Congress publishes for this page. Whole page, not a crop. The soprano-bass-alto-tenor sequence the retrieving lane quotes from this page is Library of Congress optical recognition and is NOT collated; the lane says so. Nothing may be asserted about the printing in the Farm, Field and Stockman, which this page only credits.
artifacts.rights_basis: The issue was published in the United States before 1929 and is in the public domain there; the retrieving research lane of run efff3a6f73c1f451 recorded the same finding, in the form 'nineteenth-century American newspaper digitised by the Library of Congress; public domain'. The Library of Congress's mechanical digitisation and optical recognition of a public-domain page add no original authorship of their own. The bytes are not retained on the demonstrated-size ground guidance/sources.md allows: 8.05 MB of greyscale page master, above the 5.88 MB that is the largest payload this library retains across 10,461 files. What a reader with no network opens instead is the word-coordinate index of the same page, retained beside this record, which carries the page's words though not its letterform; and that shortfall is why nothing quoted from this page in this run rises above the lane's own uncollated optical reading.
